papers.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
papers.summary: Quarterly earnings forecasting requires an agent to connect financial evidence to the income-statement line items that produce a company's reported earnings. We introduce EPSBench, a benchmark for studying this ability across 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies. papers.summary: Self-distillation offers a way to improve reasoning models when a suitable external teacher is unavailable. papers.summary: Autoregressive (AR) image generators are powerful in principle but inflexible in practice: training with a fixed raster-scan order hardcodes a single factorization of the image distribution into the model, leaving it unable to inpaint, outpaint, or edit at inference time. papers.summary: Language agents increasingly act through external tools and interactive environments, making the interface between the model and its executable capabilities part of the decision process. papers.summary: Developers download quantized large language models (LLMs) from public registries to run them locally. None of the registries we examined documented functional testing of their files. papers.summary: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. papers.summary: Blockchain forensics is adversarial and open-ended: money launderers split, swap, and bridge funds, cut their trail at mixers or custodial services, and change tactics from one incident to the next. Investigators must keep adapting their tracing in response. papers.summary: Whether models trained on different modalities converge to the same representation of the world is central to AI. papers.summary: Formula-Driven Supervised Learning (FDSL) enables vision pre-training without real images, but existing methods cast pre-training as classification on discretized labels, discarding continuity in the generative process.
